userStories.title: Add SM holdings as primary discovery source in scanner.py
userStories.description:
Current state: scanner.py at businesses/horizen-zkverify/base-trader/scripts/scanner.py discovers tokens via gt_discover_tokens() (GeckoTerminal trending pools). This is a retail/momentum signal, not an SM signal. The Nansen smart-money/holdings endpoint (added in bt-sm-signal US-001) returns what SM wallets actually hold.

What to build:
1. Add discover_sm_from_holdings(chain='base', limit=20) function:
   - Call get_sm_holdings(chain) (already cached, 0 extra credits)
   - Filter to tokens with sm_wallet_count >= 3
   - Sort by sm_wallet_count descending (most SM interest first)
   - Return list of token dicts matching the discovery format: {address, symbol, name, volume_24h, market_cap_usd, holders_count, source: 'sm_holdings'}
   - volume_24h and market_cap_usd can be 0 (will be enriched later from GeckoTerminal)

2. Update discover_sm_tokens() to merge both sources:
   - First: tokens from discover_sm_from_holdings() (SM signal, primary)
   - Second: tokens from _discover_from_screener() (screener netflow, secondary)
   - Third: tokens from gt_discover_tokens() (GeckoTerminal trending, supplement)
   - Deduplicate by address (SM source takes priority)
   - Return merged list, capped at limit

Constraints:
- Do NOT modify run_pipeline.py, signal_filter.py, or any other file
- GeckoTerminal discovery stays as a supplement — do not remove it
- Mock mode must return SM holdings tokens in the discovery list
- If get_sm_holdings() returns empty (API error), fall back to existing behavior
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -c "import sys,os; os.environ['NANSEN_MOCK']='1'; sys.path.insert(0,'businesses/horizen-zkverify/base-trader/scripts'); from scanner import discover_sm_tokens; tokens=discover_sm_tokens(); assert len(tokens)>0; sources=set(t.get('source','') for t in tokens); print(f'Sources: {sources}, count={len(tokens)} PASS')"
